title: Residential Construction Image Dataset Using CSI Divisions for Deep Learning-based Object Detection

problem.summary: Accurate recognition of construction site elements is essential for the application of deep learning (DL) in the construction industry.
statements: Accurate recognition of construction site elements is essential for the application of deep learning (DL) in the construction industry.
Despite rapid advances in computer vision, the adoption of DL in construction has been limited by the lack of structured, publicly available datasets aligned with established industry standards.

To address this gap, we introduce the Residential Construction Dataset Using CSI Divisions (ResCD-CSI) image dataset, a manually labeled image benchmark organized according to the divisional structure defined by the Construction Specifications Institute (CSI).

components: Despite rapid advances in computer vision, the adoption of DL in construction has been limited by the lack of structured, publicly available datasets aligned with established industry standards.

To address this gap, we introduce the Residential Construction Dataset Using CSI Divisions (ResCD-CSI) image dataset, a manually labeled image benchmark organized according to the divisional structure defined by the Construction Specifications Institute (CSI).

The dataset comprises high-resolution images collected from active residential construction sites across the United States, capturing diverse building components, materials, and equipment under real-world conditions.

limitations.summary: Background & Summary The construction industry remains highly labor-intensive, particularly for skilled labor, with most on-site management tasks and interventions still relying on manual judgments, which are often inefficient and difficult to scale 1.
items: Background & Summary The construction industry remains highly labor-intensive, particularly for skilled labor, with most on-site management tasks and interventions still relying on manual judgments, which are often inefficient and difficult to scale 1.

However, its practical application in this field remains constrained by a fundamental limitation, including the lack of large-scale, wellannotated, and publicly available datasets tailored to the complexity of construction environments 5 .

Several challenges drive these gaps: (1) restricted access to active sites due to safety and security concerns; (2) limited and repetitive camera perspectives that risk overfitting detection models; and (3) the inherently dynamic and chaotic nature of construction environments, which increases the difficulty and cost of data collection while demanding expert annotation 6.
